root_cause.text: In fs/ceph/dir.c, ceph_finish_lookup() and ceph_lookup() wrongly assumed a negative dentry was necessarily unhashed and called d_add(dentry, NULL) on already-hashed negative dentries, causing the VFS dcache hash node to be reinserted and corrupted.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states these two Ceph paths “incorrectly assume ‘negative’ also means ‘unhashed’,” and the patch fixes both call sites by changing unconditional d_add(dentry, NULL) to `if (d_unhashed(dentry)) d_add(dentry, NULL);`; it also explains that d_add() reaches __d_rehash(), which “unconditionally reinserts dentry->d_hash,” corrupting the hlist bucket and potentially creating a self-loop.

intent_record.intent_summary: Only add the lookup dentry as a negative dentry when it is still unhashed to avoid re-adding an already hashed dentry.
intent_record.what: The unconditional call to d_add(dentry, NULL) in the non-error lookup path was replaced with a conditional block that calls d_add(dentry, NULL) only if d_unhashed(dentry) returns true.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents adding a dentry to the dcache when it is already hashed, avoiding a redundant or invalid re-addition while still ensuring unhashed dentries are added as negative dentries when appropriate.

intent_record.what: The unconditional call to d_add(dentry, NULL) in the -ENOENT path of ceph_lookup() was changed to execute only when d_unhashed(dentry) is true, by wrapping it in an if statement.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents attempting to add a dentry that is already hashed into the dcache, while still adding negative dentries for unhashed entries. This avoids incorrect or unsafe duplicate dentry insertion during lookup completion when the target does not exist.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement unconditionally adds a negative dentry without verifying that the dentry is unhashed. In both ceph_finish_lookup() and the -ENOENT path of ceph_lookup(), that assumption is invalid for already-hashed negative dentries, so calling d_add() here can reinsert the existing dcache hash node and corrupt the VFS dcache.

bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant logic is fully visible in this snippet, specifically in both ceph_finish_lookup() and ceph_lookup(), so the code is sufficient to judge. The vulnerable construct is present because both functions call d_add(dentry, NULL) based only on the dentry being negative (dentry->d_inode == NULL / ENOENT path), without checking whether the dentry is already hashed. In ceph_finish_lookup(), under the ENOENT no-trace path: `if (!req->r_reply_info.head->is_dentry) { ... if (dentry->d_inode) { d_drop(dentry); err = -ENOENT; } else { d_add(dentry, NULL); } }`. This assumes that a negative dentry can simply be added, but the root cause says negative dentries may already be hashed, and re-calling d_add() corrupts the dcache hash node. Likewise in ceph_lookup(), the local ENOENT fast path does: `if (dentry->d_inode == NULL) { ... if (...) { ... d_add(dentry, NULL); ... return NULL; } }`, again with no unhashed check such as `d_unhashed(dentry)` and no alternate handling for already-hashed negative dentries. Therefore the buggy construct is present, and the fix is not present.
